nearest_prs.difference: Sorts clean and nailed saw offcuts into stack/tote; this task exchanges a live support under a batten and clears two plain offcuts.

nearest_prs.title: Find by touch and take out the one prop under a slab that carries nothing
nearest_prs.difference: Unloaded miniature rescue-shoring removal; this scene transfers a real-size-for-bench batten load to a replacement bearer, requires ongoing support and cleans a carpentry work area.

nearest_prs.title: Reseat a board that missed one of its two supports, without knocking over the bottle beside it
nearest_prs.difference: Ordinary placement of a board above loose blocks was the review concern; this task instead preserves an existing load path while replacing a load-bearing scrap prop, then clears the work area.

physical_skill: Maintain a batten support path while a scrap prop is removed and a proper bearer is positioned, then clear the offcuts. No particular hand order is required.
valid_shortcuts: Holding the batten and sliding the replacement bearer in before removing the prop is valid if the batten never contacts the bench.
Sliding the replacement bearer under the supported batten before removing the prop is also valid if it achieves the same measured support condition.
distinct_from_nearest: The pending offcut PR is about nail hazard sorting; the rejected prop task is unloaded and does not restore support; the rejected board task is static placement. This task requires a continuing load transfer, actual bearer contact within 2 mm, and work-area cleanup.
review_limits: Importance is supported by carpenter employment and OSHA cleanup duties; the frequency of this exact prop scenario is not claimed.
